employee_facing_sections.heading: 1. Today’s skill
employee_facing_sections.content_markdown: Distinguish four common plumbing connection types using their joining features, without assuming that similar-looking parts are compatible.

employee_facing_sections.heading: 2. Why it matters
employee_facing_sections.content_markdown: A customer may call every connection that turns a “screw-on fitting.” Recognizing how the connection actually joins helps you ask better questions before selecting a replacement.

employee_facing_sections.heading: 3. Learn it
employee_facing_sections.content_markdown:
Start with **how the parts join**, rather than the fitting’s color or overall shape.

| Connection type | Recognition clue |
|---|---|
| **Threaded pipe connection** | External threads on one part screw into matching internal threads on another. |
| **Slip joint** | Common on tubular sink drains: a nut tightens around a tube, with a washer providing the seal. |
| **Solvent weld** | A plastic pipe fits into a socket designed for joining with the appropriate solvent cement. |
| **Push-to-connect** | A compatible pipe pushes into a fitting with an internal gripping and sealing mechanism. |

Threaded pipe connections and solvent-welded connections use different joining methods. Solvent welding chemically joins compatible plastic surfaces; it is not simply a friction fit. [Source 1]

**Recommended action:** Identify the connection at **each end**. One adapter can have a slip-joint connection at one end and a solvent-weld socket at the other. Naming one end does not describe the entire fitting. [Source 2]

**Common mistake:** Seeing threads on a slip-joint nut and treating it as a threaded pipe connection. Look at the whole assembly: the tube, nut, and sealing washer.

Push-to-connect fittings may hide their working parts. For example, SharkBite describes an internal grab ring that holds the pipe and an O-ring that seals it. Do not assume every push fitting accepts the same pipe materials. [Source 3]

**When to verify or seek help:** Before recommending a replacement, confirm pipe material, size, connection type, and intended use against the specific product’s instructions. A smooth socket alone does not prove that a fitting is intended for solvent welding. If identification remains uncertain, ask a knowledgeable coworker or manufacturer representative.

employee_facing_sections.heading: 4. Customer scenario
employee_facing_sections.content_markdown:
A customer brings in a loose nut and washer from beneath a bathroom sink. Their photo shows a smooth drain tube passing through the nut into another fitting.

They ask, “What kind of connection should I look for?”

employee_facing_sections.heading: 5. Quick check
employee_facing_sections.content_markdown:
**Question ID: CD-0002-Q01**

Which connection type best matches the assembly shown and described?

A. Slip joint
B. Threaded pipe connection
C. Solvent weld
D. Push-to-connect

reviewer_sections.content_markdown:
**Actual supplied media assets:** None.

**Suggested optional media:** Four independently photographed, uninstalled example connections, with both ends visible where applicable. An exploded slip-joint example would help distinguish its nut, washer, and tube.

**Accessibility description for proposed media:** “Four labeled connection examples: mating internal and external pipe threads; a tubular drain with a separate nut and washer; a plastic solvent-weld socket; and a push-to-connect fitting. The slip-joint example labels the tube, nut, and washer.” Provide the recognition table as text; do not rely on color alone.

**Sources checked October 19, 2026:**

- [Source 1] Oatey, [Complete Guide to Pipe Fittings](https://www.oatey.com/faqs-blog-videos-case-studies/blog/complete-guide-pipe-fittings): Threaded connections and solvent-welding principles. Used only for these high-level distinctions.
- [Source 2] Oatey, [Plastic Trap Adapter, HDC9000A](https://www.oatey.com/products/p_038753005386/oatey-plastic-trap-adapter): Documents a slip-joint inlet, nut and washer, and solvent-weld outlet on one adapter.
- [Source 3] SharkBite, [See What’s Inside a SharkBite Push-to-Connect Fitting](https://www.sharkbite.com/us/en/resources/blog/service-and-repair/fitting-tips-guides/see-whats-inside-a-sharkbite-push-to-connect-fitting): Internal gripping and sealing components for the manufacturer’s described design.

### 1. Today’s skill

Distinguish four common plumbing connection types using their joining features, without assuming that similar-looking parts are compatible.

### 2. Why it matters
